# Loment 0.1.4.5

Three things land in this release. Each one was announced in
[`v0.1.4.5-pre`](https://github.com/FujoJTOP/loment/releases/tag/v0.1.4.5-pre) while it was still
being built; the parts of that announcement that were marked *in review* have landed, and the rest is
unchanged.

## Install

| Asset | |
|---|---|
| `loment-0.1.4.5-linux-x64.tar.gz` | Linux x86-64. Unpack anywhere; `bin/loment` is the launcher. |
| `loment-0.1.4.5-windows-x64.zip` | Windows x86-64. Unzip and run `install.cmd`. |
| `loment-0.1.4.5-windows-x64-setup.exe` | Windows x86-64, self-extracting. Double-click. |
| `loment-skill.zip` | The agent guide (`SKILL.md`) on its own, for people who want only that. |
| `SHA256SUMS` | Checksums. The installers verify the payload against this before copying anything. |

Installing and running needs **no Python, no clang and no WSL** — the package is native binaries plus
the standard library. `loment run hello.lomt` and you are done.

**If 0.1.4's `setup.exe` did nothing on your machine, this one installs.** That installer launched
`install.cmd` by bare file name; where `NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath` is set — developer
machines and hardened ones — `cmd` cannot find a script that way, so the package unpacked itself and
exited having installed nothing
([#117](https://github.com/FujoJTOP/loment/issues/117)). The launch command now carries the unpack
directory. The 0.1.4 asset itself is **not** being rebuilt — that would change the bytes under a
version number already in the wild — so 0.1.4 users should stay on the `zip` until they move to this
release.

## 1. LomentGC — the four-tier reclamation ladder

Reclamation in Loment is not one algorithm over one heap. Every `alloc` site is assigned, at compile
time, to one rung of a ladder, and *how much of this program's memory the collector is responsible
for* is a **number carried in the artifact**:

| Rung | What it does |
|---|---|
| `L0` | static promotion — a provably non-escaping allocation never reaches the heap at all |
| `L1` | last-use — the allocator front is returned right after the final use |
| `L2` | block epochs — a loop body, or either arm of an `if`, that allocates and drops returns its whole region at once |
| `L3` | mark-sweep with precise roots, triggered by bytes allocated |

The ladder is implemented **twice** — the reference compiler (`tools/lomentc.py`) and the
self-hosted one (`loment/selfhost/`) — and the two must agree byte for byte. The three tiers
`choose gc_manual` / `choose gc_auto` / `choose gc_auto_alpha` select how far down the ladder a unit
is allowed to go. Potato **v10** carries `gc_ladder` = `{l0, l1, l2, l3, total_sites}`, and **two
independent validators** check the arithmetic (`l0 + l1 + l2 + l3 == total_sites`) without reading a
single line of source.

The two halves of the `gc_auto_alpha` policy that were still *in review* at announcement time are in
this release: an **adaptive** threshold that follows the live set
([#200](https://github.com/FujoJTOP/loment/pull/200)) and a **generational** collector — a 1024-entry
card table, a write barrier at every `store8` site, and `minor`/`major` levels
([#230](https://github.com/FujoJTOP/loment/pull/230)). The difference to keep in mind between the
tiers is not throughput but the **ceiling**: on the heap-building example
(`loment/examples/gc_heap/`), the same linked-list walk runs to completion under `gc_auto` and
`gc_auto_alpha` and exhausts the arena under `gc_manual`. The numbers are in
[docs/210](docs/210-loment-gc-design.md) §7.

**Still open.** [docs/210](docs/210-loment-gc-design.md) §7 keeps its own list, and it is shorter than
it was but not empty: `L2` does not yet cover a function body the way it covers a loop body or an `if`
arm; `L2`'s four boundaries are the price of not resolving scopes on the token stream; there is no
debug tier; and intra-block precision needs a typed `alloc`. The allocator has a soundness hole of its
own — [#164](https://github.com/FujoJTOP/loment/issues/164): `free` does not verify ownership, so the
same block can be released twice and two live regions end up aliasing. The GC v2 design (`gc_strict`,
reclamation-by-recomputation) remains a design document, not an implementation — none of its criteria
have been run.

## 2. Networking, on both targets

The same `.lomt` source can open a socket on Linux **and** on Windows, from the same output bytes. On
ELF the calls are the Linux syscalls directly; on PE the runtime dispatches **21 numbers** through
`ws2_32`. `syscall7` fills all six argument registers, so address-carrying UDP — `sendto` /
`recvfrom`, where the sixth argument is the `socklen_t` — is expressible in the language.
`tools/loment_pe_test.py` walks the whole surface by having a program connect to itself: `socket` /
`setsockopt` / `bind` / `listen` / `getsockname` / `connect` / `accept` / `read` / `write` / `poll` /
`accept4` / IPv6.

Two boundaries, stated plainly, because they are the parts that are *not* there:

* **There is no networking library.** `std` has no `net` module; you write the syscalls yourself.
  Nothing wraps them yet.
* **There is no admission gate.** A unit that declares
  `excluded "network: 本单元不申请任何 net 能力"` (as `loment/examples/demo.lomt` does) is not stopped
  from calling `socket` — the capability check compares *domain names* and never looks at behaviour.
  [docs/218](docs/218-loment-net-admission.md) is a research draft arguing the project should have
  **no permission list at all** rather than a gate; its criteria have not been run.

The measurements are in [docs/217](docs/217-loment-socket-parity.md),
[docs/220](docs/220-syscall7-and-udp.md) and [docs/221](docs/221-loment-pe-poll.md).

## 3. lompi 0.2.0 Alpha

The package manager moves from 0.1.5 to **0.2.0 Alpha**. It is the version that can download:
`lompi fetch` reads the registry over a raw socket instead of printing a `git clone` for you to run.
What it cannot do is HTTPS or hostnames — the toolchain has no TLS and no resolver yet, so `http://`
with an IPv4 literal is the whole fetchable surface
([docs/236](docs/236-lompi-020-network.md)). The announcement lives on the package manager's own
repository, [FujoJTOP/lompi](https://github.com/FujoJTOP/lompi).

---

Loment is a **systems programming language** that compiles to native x86-64 — Linux ELF, Windows PE,
or a freestanding object for bare metal. What goes into one is the program's decision and the build
records it: `choose sealed`, the default, is an artifact with **no runtime, no libc and no undefined
symbols**.

**`choose hosted` — the dimension for artifacts that link real libc and shared libraries — is *not* in
0.1.4.5.** That path is unfinished ([docs/222](docs/222-lompi-020-foreign-libs.md) sec 4.5,
[docs/219](docs/219-world-ports.md) sec 8c), so the release toolchain refuses it by name and a release
build cannot link a foreign object that carries ports. The dimension stays writable in the development
channel, where it is being built; calling libc from a release build is not something 0.1.4.5 offers.

The toolchain is self-hosted at run time: compiling and running needs no Python, no clang and no WSL.
The language surface is frozen ([docs/158](docs/158-loment-freeze.md) says what changing it costs); the
implementation is not. What this release does **not** include is listed item by item, and was audited,
in [docs/202](docs/202-loment-014-release-gate.md).
